mainTopic: The end of the dispute about a טומטום who turned out to be a סריס, the closing of פרק על אלו מומין, and the opening of the new משנה listing blemishes that disqualify a כהן
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה about a טומטום found to be a סריס. Their views differ on whether his חליצה counts. Then the הדרן closes פרק על אלו מומין, and a new משנה teaches that every animal blemish also disqualifies a כהן, plus extra human-only blemishes such as odd head shapes, humped backs and baldness. The גמרא asks how the two lists can be the same when the תורה lists some blemishes only for animals and others only for people. It answers with a גזירה שוה from the words גרב and ילפת, and proves these words are extra. It then explains why the תורה still wrote two separate lists, using the rule of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל about repeated passages. Next, רבא shows why the תורה had to mention מום by a כהן, by קדשים and by a בכור: each has a special feature, so none can be learned from one or two of the others. Finally, רבי יוחנן derives the extra human blemishes from the verse 'מזרע אהרן': a כהן must look like the other כהנים.

steps.title: The practical difference between the two opinions about the טומטום's חליצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the dispute matters in two cases: whether his חליצה disqualifies the widow from the other brothers, and whether he must do חליצה when there are no other brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is in two cases. One case is whether his חליצה disqualifies her when there are other brothers. The other case is whether she needs חליצה from him when there are no other brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא had asked what practical difference there is between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה. Here it answers by naming two real-life cases where their views lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds this person is surely a סריס חמה, a natural-born סריס, so his חליצה has no legal effect at all. רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה holds he might not be one, so his חליצה might count. That gives two results. When there are other brothers, his חליצה would forbid her to them only according to רבי יוסי. When there are no other brothers, only רבי יוסי requires him to do חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: To disqualify. Here it means making the widow forbidden to do יבום with the other brothers.
To perform חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום.
Where there are other brothers of the dead husband.
There is a difference between them. This is the standard answer to the question of how two opinions differ in practice.
A person who was born a סריס, as opposed to one who became a סריס through an injury.

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the טומטום's חליצה means nothing. According to רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה, it might count. That one point produces both practical differences.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase לפסול does not mean that the טומטום himself is disqualified. It means his חליצה would forbid the widow from marrying the other brothers through יבום.

phrases.english: To disqualify her where there are other brothers,
phrases.notes: If this טומטום does חליצה, does that block her from doing יבום with one of the other brothers?

phrases.english: and to perform חליצה where there are no other brothers,
there is a difference between them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question מאי בינייהו that the גמרא asked just before this passage begins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר רבי יהודה regarding the טומטום found to be a סריס?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are two differences. First, whether his חליצה forbids the widow to the other brothers. Second, whether he must do חליצה when he is the only brother.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק על אלו מומין
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marks the end of the פרק על אלו מומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק על אלו מומין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק, showing that the פרק on animal blemishes is now complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words express a wish to come back and learn this פרק again. They also signal that a new topic is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the formula said when completing a פרק.
The name of the פרק just completed, which deals with blemishes in animals.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "On These Blemishes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the entire פרק after its final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק על אלו מומין is finished.

steps.title: Animal blemishes also disqualify a כהן, and there are extra human blemishes
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that every blemish that disqualifies an animal, whether permanent or temporary, also disqualifies a כהן. It then begins listing extra blemishes that apply only to people, mostly unusual head shapes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These blemishes, whether permanent or temporary, disqualify a person. In addition to them, these also disqualify: one with a pointed head, one with a turnip-shaped head, one with a hammer-shaped head, one whose head has a dent, and one whose back of the head sticks out.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It takes the whole list of animal blemishes from the last פרק and applies it to a כהן, then starts adding blemishes found only in humans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה builds directly on the previous פרק. Every animal blemish, whether permanent or temporary, disqualifies a כהן from the Temple service. The words ויתר עליהן add more blemishes that only apply to people, starting with abnormal head shapes. The list continues in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of the משנה text.
Permanent blemishes.
Temporary blemishes that can heal.
They disqualify in a person, meaning a כהן cannot serve in the Temple.
And in addition to them, meaning extra blemishes beyond the animal list.
One whose head is pointed: narrow on top and wide below.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole new פרק. The rules for a blemished כהן are built on top of the animal blemish rules, with human-only blemishes added.

phrases.english: משנה: These blemishes,
phrases.notes: He means all the animal blemishes listed in the previous פרק.

phrases.english: whether permanent or temporary,
disqualify in a person,
phrases.notes: The person here is a כהן, who cannot do the Temple service with these blemishes.

phrases.english: and in addition to them:
one with a pointed head, and one with a turnip-shaped head,
and one with a hammer-shaped head, and one whose head has a dent,
and one whose back of the head sticks out.

steps.triggerLanguage: מתני׳ מומין אלו בין קבועין בין עוברים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן. It applies the previous פרק's animal blemishes to a כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All animal blemishes, permanent or temporary, disqualify a כהן. There are also extra human-only blemishes, beginning with abnormal head shapes.

steps.title: The משנה continues: a humped back and baldness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of human-only blemishes. It records a dispute about humpbacked people, and it defines when a bald כהן is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Humpbacked people: רבי יהודה says they are fit, and the חכמים say they are disqualified. A bald person is disqualified. Who counts as bald? Anyone who does not have a strip of hair going around from ear to ear. If he has such a strip, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing blemishes that apply only to a כהן. It adds a humped back, which is under dispute, and baldness, which comes with a clear definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a humped back, רבי יהודה does not count it as a blemish, but the חכמים do. Baldness disqualifies a כהן, and the משנה gives a measurable test for it: a ring of hair from ear to ear around the back of the head makes him fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Humpbacked people, with a hump on the back
Rules fit or valid
Rule disqualified
A bald person
A strip or row of hair

phrases.english: And those with humped backs:
Rabbi Yehuda deems them fit, and the Rabbis disqualify them.
A bald person is disqualified.
Who is considered bald?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שִׁיטָה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר
phrases.english: Anyone who does not have a strip of hair
going around from ear to ear;
phrases.notes: Picture a band of hair circling the back of the head, from one ear to the other.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: if he has one, he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַעֲלֵי חֲטָרוֹת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of human-only blemishes that began in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Humped backs are disputed: רבי יהודה rules them fit and the חכמים rule them disqualified. A bald כהן is disqualified unless he has a ring of hair from ear to ear.

steps.title: How can all animal blemishes apply to people when the lists differ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's opening rule. Some blemishes appear in the תורה only for animals and others only for people, so how can the two lists be treated as the same?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה say this? There is a wart, which the תורה does not write for a person. And also, דק and תבלול are not written for an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion by challenging the משנה's claim that every blemish that disqualifies an animal also disqualifies a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists a wart (יבלת) only for animals, and דק and תבלול (eye blemishes) only for a כהן. So the two lists do not match, and the משנה's assumption that they are the same seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
A wart
An eye blemish, often understood as a film or cataract
An eye blemish where the white of the eye intrudes on the iris

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
phrases.notes: He is asking why the משנה says every animal blemish also disqualifies a כהן.

phrases.english: But there is a wart,
which is not written in the Torah regarding a person!
phrases.notes: It is written for animals in ויקרא 22:22.

phrases.english: And furthermore: a cataract and tevallul,
which are not written regarding an animal!
phrases.notes: They are written for a כהן in ויקרא 21:20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by challenging the משנה's general rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that every animal blemish also disqualifies a כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה's lists differ: יבלת is written only for animals, and דק and תבלול only for people. So the two lists cannot simply be treated as one.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה links the two lists
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that each list is learned from the other. A ברייתא derives this from the words גרב and ילפת, which appear in both lists, through a גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn from each other, as a ברייתא teaches: For a person, a wart is not mentioned. For an animal, דק and תבלול are not mentioned. How do we know to apply what is said about one to the other, and what is said about the other to the first? The verse says 'scabbed' and 'scabbed,' 'scurvy' and 'scurvy,' to make a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Since the same words appear in both lists, a גזירה שוה joins them into one combined list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words גרב and ילפת are written both for a כהן and for an animal. Because the same words appear in both places, a גזירה שוה moves the wart over to people and moves דק and תבלול over to animals, so the two lists become identical.

keyTerms.meaning: From each other
A scab or dry itch, a skin blemish
A type of skin disease, often translated as scurvy
Linking two laws because the same word appears in both

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that people and animals share one combined list of blemishes.

phrases.english: They are derived from one another,
as it is taught:
Regarding a person, a wart is not stated of him;
regarding an animal, a cataract and tevallul are not stated.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what is said of this one to that one,
and what is said of that one to this one?
The verse states: 'scabbed' and 'scabbed,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:20 and ויקרא 22:22.

phrases.english: 'scurvy' and 'scurvy,' for a verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source derivation through a גזירה שוה from a ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each list stands alone, so the משנה's rule has no source.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared words גרב and ילפת join the lists, so every blemish on one list applies to the other.

steps.title: The words must be extra, or the analogy could be refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that this גזירה שוה works only if the words are extra (מופנה). Otherwise, real differences between people and animals could break the comparison in both directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words must be free. If they were not free, the analogy could be refuted: you could not learn a person from an animal, because the animal itself is offered on the מזבח. And you could not learn an animal from a person, because a person is included in the מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to the answer: the shared words have to be extra. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will show that they really are extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גזירה שוה can be broken by showing a real difference between the two cases. Here there are differences in both directions: an animal is stricter because it is itself offered on the מזבח, and a person is stricter because he is obligated in מצוות. Only if the words are extra does the comparison hold despite these differences.

keyTerms.meaning: Free or extra, meaning the words are not needed for anything else and are written for the comparison
To refute or break the argument
The altar
Was included in the commandments, meaning obligated in מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is rejecting the גזירה שוה here. It is only saying the comparison needs extra words, and it will next show that the words really are extra.

phrases.english: They are free,
phrases.notes: Meaning these words are extra in the פסוק, there just to make the comparison.

phrases.english: for if they were not free, one could refute it:
A person cannot be derived from an animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הִיא עַצְמָהּ קְרֵיבָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ;
phrases.english: since it itself is sacrificed upon the altar;
an animal cannot be derived from a person,
since he was included in the מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְנֵי, דְּאִי לָא מַפְנֵי, אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the גזירה שוה from step 6 and sets up the proof that the words are extra.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת must rest on extra words, because without that each side could be distinguished from the other.

steps.title: Proving that the words are truly extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that גרב is extra. A קל וחומר from ילפת would already teach that גרב is a blemish, so the word גרב was written only to free it for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, the words really are extra. The תורה could have written only ילפת and left out גרב. I would have reasoned: if ילפת, which is not repulsive, counts as a blemish, then surely גרב, which is repulsive, does. So why did the תורה write גרב? To leave it free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry from the last step by proving that the word גרב is extra and free for learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה can be broken by real differences between people and animals unless its words are extra. Here, a קל וחומר from ילפת to גרב shows that writing גרב adds no new law. That makes it extra, so the comparison holds.

keyTerms.meaning: They are definitely extra (free), so they can be used for a גזירה שוה
A skin disease (scurvy-like) that is not repulsive
A scab disease that is repulsive
Repulsive, disgusting
All the more so (the language of a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת stands, because גרב is extra. A קל וחומר from ילפת would already have taught it.

phrases.english: Indeed, they are definitely extra (free).
Let the Merciful One write "scurvy"
and "scab" would not be needed,
and I would say:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה יַלֶּפֶת דְּלָא מְאִיסָא הָוֵי מוּמָא,
phrases.english: If scurvy, which is not repulsive, is a blemish,
then scab, which is repulsive, all the more so!
So why do I need the "scab" that the Merciful One wrote?
phrases.notes: גרב appears twice: once for כהנים (ויקרא 21:20) and once for animals (ויקרא 22:22).

phrases.english: To leave it free (for the גזירה שוה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the condition raised in step 7 by showing the words really are extra
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the word is extra because a קל וחומר already teaches its law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the words are needed for their own law, so the גזירה שוה could be broken
steps.terutzMaskana: גרב is extra, so the גזירה שוה cannot be broken

steps.title: Why not write the whole list only once?
steps.stepSummary: If each list is learned from the other, the תורה could have written every blemish in one place, put גרב and ילפת in both places, and let the second case learn everything from the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the תורה write all the blemishes in just one place, write גרב and ילפת in both places, and let the other case be learned from that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges why the תורה bothered to write two long lists when one list plus the גזירה שוה would be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גזירה שוה makes the two lists equal, writing the shared blemishes twice seems wasteful. Only the linking words גרב and ילפת would need to appear in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them in one place
Here and here, meaning in both places
And let them be learned from the one

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write all of them in one place,
and write scab and scurvy here and here,
and let them be learned from the one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the גזירה שוה is secure, the גמרא questions why both lists are needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The תורה's choice to write full blemish lists for both people and animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the גזירה שוה links the lists, one full list plus the linking words should be enough

steps.title: If the full list were written only for people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: in which case would it be written? Had it been written only for people, we would think only people's blemishes apply to animals. Then animal-only blemishes like קלוט would not disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: In which of the two should the תורה write the full list? If it were written for a person, I would say: whatever disqualifies a person disqualifies an animal. But קלוט and חוטין, which do not exist in people, would not disqualify an animal either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by showing what would go wrong if the full list appeared only for כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blemishes exist only in animals, such as closed hooves. A list written for people could never include them. So we would assume they do not disqualify animals either.

keyTerms.meaning: On which one, in which one
An animal whose hooves are closed, not split
A blemish of the gums, found only in animals
They do not exist (in that case)

phrases.english: In which one should the Merciful One write them?
If it had written them for a person,
I would have said:
Whatever disqualifies a person disqualifies an animal,
but closed hooves and gums, which do not exist in a person,
would not disqualify in an animal either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9, starting with the option of writing the list for people
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that writing only one list would leave out blemishes unique to the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One list for people would be enough
steps.terutzMaskana: A list only for people would lose the animal-only blemishes

steps.title: If the full list were written only for animals
steps.stepSummary: Writing the full list only for animals fails too. Then people-only blemishes like גבן and חרום would not disqualify a כהן. So both lists are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה wrote all of them for an animal, I would say: whatever disqualifies an animal disqualifies a person. But גבן and חרום, which do not exist in animals, would not disqualify a person either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing that the other option, writing everything for animals, fails as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blemishes, like a sunken nose, appear only in people. A list written only for animals would miss them. Since each option leaves something out, the תורה had to write lists in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with a blemish of the eyebrows
A person with a sunken (flat) nose
Also, either

steps.whatToRemember: Each list holds blemishes that cannot exist in the other case. So neither list alone could teach everything, and the תורה wrote both.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One wrote all of them for an animal,
I would have said:
Whatever disqualifies an animal disqualifies a person,
but a gibben and a ḥarum, which do not exist in an animal,
would not disqualify in a person either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 10 by testing the second option
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the second option also leaves out unique blemishes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One list for animals would be enough
steps.terutzMaskana: Both lists are needed, because each holds blemishes unique to its own case

steps.title: Why not write the shared blemishes only once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a shorter way the תורה could have written the lists: shared blemishes once, unique blemishes in their own place, and only גרב and ילפת in both places to make the גזירה שוה work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write all the shared blemishes in one place. The ones that apply only to animals, it should write by animals. The ones that apply only to people, it should write by people. גרב and ילפת should be written in both places, and the two cases would learn from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: Steps 10–11 showed that each list has unique blemishes, so both lists are needed. Now the גמרא asks: fine, but why repeat the shared blemishes in both lists?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in steps 10–11 only explained why each list needs its own unique items. It did not explain why the shared items appear twice. The proposal: write shared items once, write unique items separately, and keep גרב and ילפת in both places as the link for the גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: In one place
They are not found in the other one
Here and here, in both places
Let them learn from each other

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same question as step 9. Step 9 asked why not write everything in one place. Here the גמרא already accepts that unique blemishes need their own lists. It is only asking why the shared ones are repeated.

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write all of them in one place,
phrases.notes: "All of them" here means all the blemishes that people and animals share.

phrases.english: and those that are not found in the other —
let the Merciful One write them by an animal,
and those that are not found in the other —
let it write them by a person,
and גרב and ילפת — here and here,
phrases.notes: These two stay in both lists because they are the matching words for the גזירה שוה (steps 6–8).

phrases.english: and let them learn from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the challenge after steps 10–11 explained why each list must exist.
steps.kashyaTarget: The repetition of shared blemishes in both the כהן list and the animal list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Steps 10–11 justify writing the unique blemishes separately, but not repeating the shared ones. A shorter text would teach the same laws.

steps.title: A passage may be repeated just to teach something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the rule of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: when the תורה repeats a passage, it does so for the sake of the new detail in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it follows the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, who taught: any passage that was said and then said again was repeated only for the new thing that was added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this is simply how the תורה writes. It repeats a whole passage even when only one part is new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shared blemishes appear again because the תורה wanted to add the unique blemishes. It is the תורה's style to restate the whole passage, not just the new part. So the repetition of the shared items does not mean they need their own separate lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the study hall of רבי ישמעאל
Was said and then repeated
Something new that was added

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of רבי ישמעאל's school: when the תורה repeats a passage, the repetition exists for its new detail. The repeated parts are not extra and need no separate lesson.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule for reading repeated passages in the תורה. It is used in many places in ש"ס.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל,
as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Every passage that was said and then repeated —
was repeated only
for the sake of the new thing added in it.
phrases.notes: Here the "new things" are the blemishes unique to each list, like קלוט for animals or גבן for a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle of how the תורה is written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating the shared blemishes seems unnecessary, since they could be written once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה repeats a whole passage in order to add the new, unique blemishes. So the repetition is normal and needs no special explanation.

steps.title: Why does the תורה mention מום three times?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the תורה writes the law of מום separately for a person (a כהן), for קדשים, and for a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why do I need the Merciful One to write a blemish by a person, a blemish by קדשים, and a blemish by a בכור?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. Why does the תורה teach that a מום disqualifies in three separate places?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one place taught that a מום disqualifies, maybe the others could be learned from it. רבא asks why we need all three. His answer, in the next steps, will show that each case has something special, so none can be learned from another.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it?
A physical blemish
Animals set aside as קרבנות
A firstborn animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: רבא said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote

phrases.aramaic: מוּם בְּאָדָם, מוּם בְּקָדָשִׁים, מוּם בִּבְכוֹר?
phrases.english: a blemish by a person, a blemish by sacrificial animals, a blemish by a firstborn?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the two blemish lists ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the law of מום is written three separate times, instead of learning two of the cases from one

steps.title: A person's case alone would not teach animals
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that all three are needed. If the תורה wrote מום only by a person, we would say it applies only to people, because people have more מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If the Merciful One had written a blemish only by a person, I would say it applies only there, since a person has more מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer with the first reason. The person's case cannot teach the animal cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person is commanded in many מצוות, which gives him a special, higher status. So the תורה might demand that a person be free of blemishes, without demanding it of animals. That is why the animal cases must be written too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; each one is needed
Since; because this case has something special
He was given more מצוות

phrases.aramaic: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא מוּם בְּאָדָם,
phrases.english: It is necessary, for if the Merciful One had written a blemish by a person,
since he was given more מצוות.
phrases.notes: The גמרא leaves out the end: so I would say only a person is disqualified by a blemish, not animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא מוּם בְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first part of the answer to רבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The person's case cannot teach the animal cases, because a person's extra מצוות make his case special.

steps.title: A בכור cannot teach the law for a person
steps.stepSummary: Going the other way, the law for a person cannot be learned from a בכור, because a בכור itself is brought on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person cannot be learned from a firstborn animal, since the animal itself is offered on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the second reason. The בכור case cannot teach the person's case either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור has its own special strictness: the animal itself goes up on the מזבח. A כהן only serves there; he is not offered. So a blemish might disqualify a בכור without disqualifying a כהן. The person's case must therefore be written on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: Cannot be learned from
Is offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: A person cannot be learned from a firstborn animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הוּא עַצְמוֹ קָרֵב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: since it itself is offered on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer in the opposite direction, from animal to person.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור case cannot teach the person's case, because a בכור is itself offered on the מזבח, which makes it stricter.

steps.title: Offerings cannot be learned from a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Finishing the case where the תורה wrote מום only by a בכור: we could not learn קדשים from it, because a בכור is holy from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The law for קדשים cannot be learned from a בכור, because a בכור's holiness comes from the womb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second scenario: if the תורה had written מום only by a בכור, we still could not apply it to other קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed that a person cannot be learned from a בכור. Now the גמרא adds that קדשים cannot be learned from it either. A בכור is holy from the moment it is born, with no one needing to sanctify it. Regular offerings only become holy when their owner sanctifies them, so a בכור is a 'stronger' case.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, holy from birth
Animals sanctified as offerings
It cannot be learned (literally: it does not come)
From the womb, from birth

phrases.english: Offerings cannot be learned from a firstborn,
since its holiness is from the womb.
phrases.notes: A בכור becomes holy on its own at birth. Other offerings only become holy when someone sanctifies them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בכור scenario begun in step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קדשים cannot be derived from בכור because a בכור's holiness is from birth

steps.title: Neither a person nor a firstborn can be learned from offerings
steps.stepSummary: Third scenario: if the תורה wrote מום only by קדשים, we could not learn a person from it, since offerings go on the מזבח, and we could not learn a בכור from it, since offerings have greater holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person cannot be learned from קדשים, because the offerings themselves are brought on the מזבח. A בכור cannot be learned from קדשים, because their holiness is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the last option. If the תורה had written מום only by קדשים, could we learn the other two cases from it? It shows that we could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two problems here. A person is never brought on the מזבח, but קדשים are, so blemishes might matter more for them. Regular קדשים also have 'greater holiness' than a בכור, because there are many kinds of offerings, while a בכור has only one kind of holiness. So a בכור cannot be learned from them either.

keyTerms.meaning: Are brought as offerings on the מזבח
Its holiness is greater

steps.whatToRemember: Every single case has a special feature, so none of the three can be learned from just one other case.

phrases.english: A person cannot be learned from offerings,
since they themselves are offered up.
phrases.notes: A כהן serves at the מזבח but is not offered on it. The animal itself is.

phrases.english: A firstborn cannot be learned from offerings,
since its holiness is greater.
phrases.notes: "Its" means the offering's holiness. There are many kinds of offerings, but a בכור has only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the third and final scenario of רבא's answer
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither אדם nor בכור can be derived from קדשים

steps.title: Learn one case from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even if one case cannot come from one other case, why not learn one case from the other two together?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, one cannot be learned from one. But let one be learned from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. It suggests that two cases together could teach the third, so one of the three verses should be unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each single case has its own weak point. When two cases are put together, though, the special feature of one is often missing in the other. Then the law looks like it applies generally, and the third case could be learned from them. If that works, the תורה would not need to write all three.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one
Let one be learned from two

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one,
but let one be learned from two?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion that all three verses are needed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that all three verses are necessary
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Combining two cases cancels out each one's unique feature, so the third could be derived

steps.title: A firstborn cannot be learned from a person and offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no good pair to learn from. A בכור cannot come from a person and קדשים, because both have greater holiness and both apply to ordinary, non-firstborn cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which ones should it be learned? Should the תורה not write it by a בכור, and we learn it from these two? But what about these: their holiness is greater, and they apply to ordinary ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins rejecting the suggestion by checking each possible pair. Here it shows that a בכור cannot be learned from a person and קדשים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person and קדשים share two features that a בכור does not have. Both have 'greater holiness': a person has many מצוות, and there are many kinds of קדשים. Both also apply to ordinary cases, since any כהן and any animal offering count, not only firstborns. So the law might be limited to cases like theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: From which should it be learned?
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
What about these? (pointing out a special feature)
Ordinary ones, not firstborn

steps.confusionAlert: "מהי תיתי" is not a real question. It is the גמרא's way of saying "there is no pair it could come from," and then it proves this pair by pair.

phrases.english: From which should it be learned?!
Should the Merciful One not write it about a firstborn,
and let it be learned from these?
phrases.notes: "These" means a person (a כהן) and קדשים.

phrases.english: What about these:
their holiness is greater,
and they apply to ordinary ones.
phrases.notes: Blemishes disqualify any כהן and any offering, not just firstborns.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֵי תֵּיתֵי לָא לִכְתֹּב רַחֲמָנָא בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the 'one from two' challenge
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects deriving בכור from אדם and קדשים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share greater holiness and apply to non-firstborns, which a בכור lacks

steps.title: Offerings cannot be learned from a person and a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Next pair: קדשים cannot be learned from a person and a בכור, because both of those are holy on their own, without anyone sanctifying them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should it not be written by קדשים, and we learn it from these? But what about these: their holiness comes by itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the second pair. It shows that קדשים cannot be learned from a person and a בכור together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is a כהן because he is born to a כהן, and a בכור is holy because it is born first. Neither needs anyone to make it holy. קדשים only become holy when their owner sanctifies them, so they lack this shared feature and cannot be learned from the pair.

keyTerms.meaning: Their holiness comes by itself

phrases.english: About offerings, and let it be learned from these?
phrases.notes: The words "should the תורה not write it" carry over from the last step. "These" now means a person and a בכור.

phrases.english: What about these:
their holiness comes by itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues rejecting the 'one from two' challenge with the second pair
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects deriving קדשים from אדם and בכור
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources are holy automatically, while קדשים need to be sanctified

steps.title: A person cannot be learned from a firstborn and offerings together
steps.stepSummary: Last pair: if the תורה had not written מום by a person, we could not learn it from בכור and קדשים, because those are themselves brought on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Let the תורה not write it] by a person, and let us learn it from these two? No. These two have something special: they themselves are offered on the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the third and final pair. It asks whether the rule for a person could come from בכור and קדשים together, and it rejects the idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a בכור and קדשים are actually brought on the מזבח. A כהן only serves at the מזבח; he is never offered on it. Because both animals share a stricter feature that a person lacks, the person's blemishes could not be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it come, meaning let it be learned
From those, meaning the other two cases
They are offered as sacrifices
On the altar

phrases.english: [Let it not be written] by a person, and let it come from those?
phrases.notes: The words "should the תורה not write it" carry over from step 20. 'Those' means בכור and קדשים.

phrases.english: What about those:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הֵן עַצְמָן קְרֵיבִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ!
phrases.english: they themselves are offered on the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final pair after steps 20 and 21
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Learning a person's blemishes from בכור and קדשים together
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources are offered on the מזבח, which is a stricter feature that a person lacks

steps.title: All three cases had to be written
steps.stepSummary: Since no case can be learned from the others, the תורה had to write מום by a person, by a בכור and by קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole discussion. Each of the three verses about blemishes is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every attempt to learn one case from another case, or from the other two together, failed. Each case has its own special feature. So none of the three verses is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed, meaning each verse is necessary

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה wrote מום three times (by a כהן, a בכור and קדשים) because each case has a unique feature, so none could be learned from the others.

phrases.english: They are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the צריכותא after all the pairs were rejected
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three passages about blemishes are needed

steps.title: Source for the extra blemishes of a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a person has blemishes beyond those of animals, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In addition to these, there are more blemishes for a person.' Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes the משנה and asks for the source of the extra blemishes that apply only to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a כהן can be disqualified by blemishes that would not disqualify an animal. The גמרא wants a verse that shows a person has a wider list.

keyTerms.meaning: In addition to them, meaning more than the animal blemishes
From where are these words learned?

phrases.english: Beyond those, by a person.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: a כהן has more blemishes than an animal does.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic, returning to a line in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind the extra blemishes of a כהן

steps.title: A כהן must look like the rest of אהרן's descendants
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the verse 'any man of the seed of אהרן who has a blemish' that a כהן must be equal to, meaning look like, the other כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The verse says, 'Any man of the seed of אהרן who has a blemish.' This means a man who is equal among the seed of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question and gives the verse that is the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the words 'מזרע אהרן' as a requirement that the כהן be like the rest of אהרן's descendants. So even a feature that is not a real defect disqualifies him if it makes him look different from other כהנים. That is why a person has more blemishes than an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of אהרן, meaning the כהנים
Equal or similar
As the verse says

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the list of blemishes for a כהן is wider: the standard is looking like other כהנים, not only being physically damaged.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
As the verse states:
"Any man who has a blemish
of the seed of Aaron",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:21

phrases.english: A man who is equal among the seed of Aaron.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן has to look like the other כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'מזרע אהרן' requires a כהן to look like the other כהנים, so features that make him look different also disqualify him
